PAPERS.short: Espinoza-Guillen Lima case-crossover PM2.5 asthma ED road proximity 2026
PAPERS.title: Ambient fine particulate matter and asthma emergency visits in Lima, Peru: Does Residential Proximity to Major Roads Matter?
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5 from a 1x1 km multi-source model at geocoded residence
PAPERS.endpoint: Asthma emergency department visits, lag 0-15 d
PAPERS.affil: Johns Hopkins University, USA; Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia, Peru
PAPERS.n: Time-stratified case-crossover of 75,602 asthma ED visits (mean age 16.2 y) at 10 Lima public hospitals, 2017-2023, with DLNM. At lag 0, PM2.5 rising from 5 to 15 ug/m3 gave OR 1.09 (1.01-1.16); the exposure-response curve was steeper at low concentrations. Cumulative lag 0-15 OR was 4.02 (1.97-8.19) within 400 m of a major road versus 1.66 (0.81-3.38) beyond it (interaction p=0.04). The cumulative ORs are for a contrast the abstract does not state and are implausibly large for a 15-day DLNM sum; the road modifier probably carries unmodelled traffic NO2 and ultrafine particles that a 1-km PM2.5 surface cannot resolve. Relevance: direct - a near-road gradient finer than the exposure grid is exactly what curbside low-cost nodes would test.

PAPERS.short: Kim Korea urban forest PM2.5 stable isotopes receptor model seasonal 2026
PAPERS.title: Seasonal variation in urban PM(2.5) sources and the modulating role of urban forests.
PAPERS.pm: Filter PM2.5 with d13C and d15N isotopes, transects from expressway and industrial edge into forest
PAPERS.endpoint: Seasonal PM2.5, isotopic source signatures, vegetation index
PAPERS.affil: Seoul National University, South Korea; Seoul National University, South Korea
PAPERS.n: Two urban-forest regions (Gomae, expressway-to-forest transect; Sihwa, industrial complex to residential with a forest buffer) sampled across seasons with PM2.5 mass, stable carbon and nitrogen isotopes, meteorology and a vegetation index, plus receptor modelling. d15N pointed to vehicle emissions in both regions, rising in Sihwa in winter consistent with coal. Forest-interior PM2.5 was significantly lower in the growing season, but the difference vanished in the non-growing season, even under evergreen canopy, when concentrations are highest. No effect sizes, site counts or sampling durations are given; two regions cannot separate canopy from distance-to-source decay. Relevance: indirect - transect designs like this are cheap to densify with paired low-cost nodes and would resolve the season-by-canopy interaction properly.

PAPERS.short: Kim New Mexico Wyoming coal miners self-reported dust SARS-CoV-2 seroconversion 2026
PAPERS.title: Novel Occupational and Environmental Risk Factors for SARS-CoV-2 Infection Among Coal Miners: Longitudinal Cohort Study.
PAPERS.pm: Self-reported occupational dust, residential wood burning and shared transport frequency
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident anti-nucleocapsid IgG seroconversion over 12 months
PAPERS.affil: University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center, USA; University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center, USA
PAPERS.n: 230 surface coal miners (New Mexico 169, Wyoming 61), February 2021-March 2022, nucleocapsid IgG at 0, 3, 6 and 12 months. Higher self-reported mining-dust exposure was associated with lower odds of incident seroconversion, adjusted OR 0.42 (0.17-1.07), non-significant; wood burning and shared transport showed no association, and no frequent wood burner seroconverted (0/35). The hypothesis that particulate exposure raises infection risk via ACE2 upregulation was not supported. Exposure is a single questionnaire answer with no dust measurement, Firth-penalised models on few events, and vaccination plus prevalent seropositivity confound strongly. Relevance: weak - a negative occupational result resting entirely on perceived dust, a case for personal samplers in mining cohorts.

PAPERS.short: Ba rat intratracheal PM2.5 IL-17A TXNIP NLRP3 cardiac fibrosis 2026
PAPERS.title: Neutralization of IL-17A Ameliorates PM2.5-Induced Cardiac Inflammation and Fibrosis in Rats by Suppressing the TXNIP/NLRP3 Signaling Pathway.
PAPERS.pm: Collected PM2.5 by intratracheal instillation; dose not stated in the abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: Cardiac function, fibrosis, TXNIP/NLRP3 pyroptosis markers
PAPERS.affil: First Hospital of Anhui University of Science and Technology, China; First Hospital of Anhui University of Science and Technology, China
PAPERS.n: Rat cardiac-injury model by intratracheal PM2.5 instillation with an IL-17A-neutralising antibody arm, plus neonatal rat cardiac fibroblasts in vitro. PM2.5 raised splenic Th17 fraction and cardiac IL-17A/TRAF6, impaired cardiac function, and increased collagen I/III, alpha-SMA, NF-kB activation, IL-6, IL-1b, TXNIP and NLRP3-pyroptosis proteins (ASC, cleaved caspase-1, GSDMD-N, IL-18); antibody neutralisation reversed these. TXNIP knockdown abolished IL-17A effects in fibroblasts. No dose, particle source, group size or effect magnitude is reported in the abstract, and bolus instillation is far from inhaled ambient dose rates, so the human-relevant dose is unknown. Relevance: indirect - mechanism for cardiac endpoints; adds nothing to measurement.

PAPERS.short: Zareba systematic review PM neurological health older adults 21 studies 2026
PAPERS.title: Impact of Particulate Matter Exposure on Neurological Health in Older Adults: A Systematic Review.
PAPERS.pm: Long- and short-term PM2.5, PM10 and constituents as reported by included studies
PAPERS.endpoint: Cognitive decline, MCI, dementia, Alzheimer and Parkinson outcomes
PAPERS.affil: AGH University of Krakow, Poland; AGH University of Krakow, Poland
PAPERS.n: PRISMA review of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and ScienceDirect to January 2026; 21 observational studies in older adults. Cognitive performance, decline and MCI were the most studied outcomes, with several adverse associations for long-term PM2.5; dementia and Alzheimer evidence came from large cohorts but varied with exposure metric and endpoint; Parkinson hospitalisation, amyloid burden, retinal neurodegeneration and constituent-specific findings rested on one or a few studies. No pooled estimate, no risk-of-bias grading in the abstract, and 21 studies is a narrow catch for a field with dozens of large dementia cohorts, so the search or eligibility was restrictive. Relevance: indirect - restates that exposure-assessment heterogeneity, not absence of signal, limits the neuro evidence.

PAPERS.short: Lin Taiwan metro track maintenance respirable dust metals noise WBGT task-based 2026
PAPERS.title: Exposure to dust, metals, noise, and heat stress among metro track maintenance workers: task-based onsite measurements in two urban metro systems.
PAPERS.pm: Personal respirable dust and particulate metals (gravimetric) plus task-tagged real-time particle counts
PAPERS.endpoint: Task-level respirable dust, metals, noise, WBGT
PAPERS.affil: Linkou Chang Gung Memorial Hospital, Taiwan; Linkou Chang Gung Memorial Hospital, Taiwan
PAPERS.n: Seven personal sampling events across an underground high-capacity and a half-open medium-capacity Taiwanese metro, covering track cutting, aluminothermic welding and grinding. Task-duration respirable dust ranged <0.10-1.72 mg/m3, with short grinding samples to 5.71 mg/m3; cutting noise reached 106.7 dBA LAeq and peak 122.7 dB; welding WBGT peaked at 27.4 C. Results are descriptive at task-episode level because real-time records are not independent; one system per environment and day-versus-night sampling confound site contrasts, and seven events cannot support exceedance statistics. Metal speciation values are not in the abstract. Relevance: indirect - task-tagged real-time photometry against gravimetric respirable dust is the occupational analogue of sensor co-location, but no photometer-to-filter agreement is reported.

PAPERS.short: Li Shandong ICU cardiac surgery PM2.5 hospital-acquired pneumonia DLNM 2026
PAPERS.title: Association between short-term fine particulate matter exposure and hospital-acquired pneumonia risk in critically ill post-cardiac surgery patients: a 10-year cohort study using distributed lag non-linear models.
PAPERS.pm: City-level daily PM2.5 from public monitoring data (mean 59 ug/m3)
PAPERS.endpoint: Hospital-acquired pneumonia (CDC/NHSN) after cardiac surgery
PAPERS.affil: Shandong Provincial Hospital, China; Shandong Provincial Hospital, China
PAPERS.n: 6,196 post-cardiac-surgery ICU patients at one Shandong hospital, 2014-2023; 1,938 (31.3%) developed HAP. With DLNM adjusted for co-pollutants, trend and weather, PM2.5 at 30 versus 10 ug/m3 gave 14.2% higher odds of HAP at lag 1 (95% CI 2.6-27%), stronger at age >=60, BMI >23.9 and with diabetes, and robust to ventilation duration. The exposure is ambient city-wide PM2.5 assigned to patients inside an ICU, whose indoor air is filtered and decoupled from outdoors; the association may instead reflect seasonal case-mix, staffing or infection-control variation tracking pollution. Relevance: indirect - an indoor clinical endpoint fitted to outdoor monitors; an ICU indoor sensor would test the pathway directly.

PAPERS.short: Sangkham Upper Northern Thailand PM2.5 hazard quotient biomass burning 2021-2023
PAPERS.title: Spatial assessment of PM(2.5) exposure and health risks in Upper Northern Thailand: Implications for public health.
PAPERS.pm: Monitoring-station PM2.5 across eight provinces, 2021-2023
PAPERS.endpoint: Non-carcinogenic hazard quotient against WHO, US NAAQS and Thai NEB benchmarks
PAPERS.affil: University of Phayao, Thailand; Mahidol University, Thailand
PAPERS.n: Eight Upper Northern Thai provinces, 2021-2023: regional mean PM2.5 27.57 +/- 23.40 ug/m3 (8.40-78.64). Hazard quotients rose from wet to dry (biomass-burning) season: 1.19 to 4.31 against WHO, 0.50 to 1.80 against US NAAQS, 0.24 to 0.86 against Thai NEB. A hazard quotient is the concentration divided by a guideline, so these numbers restate exceedance rather than estimate risk, and the choice of benchmark alone moves the conclusion across 1. Station coverage in mountain valleys, where burning smoke pools, is not described. Relevance: indirect - northern Thailand is a region where sparse reference stations and strong valley gradients make a dense low-cost network the obvious complement.

PAPERS.short: Bonilla California CMAQ wildfire PM2.5 evaluation 2008-2018 random forest diagnostic
PAPERS.title: Evaluating CMAQ Representation of Wildfire PM2.5 in California (2008-2018): Regime-Dependent Performance and Nonlinear Error Structure.
PAPERS.pm: Daily CMAQ total and fire-only PM2.5 paired with monitor observations, June-October
PAPERS.endpoint: Bias, RMSE, event detection at 12 and 35 ug/m3
PAPERS.n: Preprint. 187,051 paired site-days across California fire seasons 2008-2018 (18 CMAQ values above 557 ug/m3 quarantined). Observed and modelled means 10.69 and 9.29 ug/m3; r 0.502, mean bias -1.40, RMSE 9.96 ug/m3. CMAQ detected 45.4% of observed site-days above 12 and 40.8% above 35 ug/m3, and at 35 it produced more events overall yet missed 1,273 of 2,151 observed ones because events did not coincide by site-day. A random forest using fire-only CMAQ PM2.5 among its predictors reached R2 0.711, RMSE 5.82 on a held-out site-year partition. The diagnostic does not apportion error to emissions, plume rise or meteorology. Relevance: direct - quantifies why model-only smoke exposure misclassifies acute days; sensor-network fusion is the fix.

PAPERS.short: Zhang SMR multi-omics PM2.5-annotated genes diabetic nephropathy TNF NOS2 methylation 2026
PAPERS.title: A multi-omics Mendelian randomization framework identifies PM2.5-annotated candidate regulatory genes and methylation-linked pathways in diabetic nephropathy.
PAPERS.pm: No exposure measurement; genes annotated as PM2.5-responsive from curated databases, plus in vitro PM2.5 exposure
PAPERS.endpoint: Genetically predicted diabetic nephropathy susceptibility
PAPERS.affil: Guang'anmen Hospital, China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences, China; Guang'anmen Hospital, China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences, China
PAPERS.n: Summary-data MR integrating eQTL, pQTL and mQTL with diabetic nephropathy GWAS, restricted to a curated set of PM2.5-annotated genes. Ten genes (TNF, NOS2, DUSP1 among them) showed genetically predicted effects; colocalisation supported a shared variant only at EIF2AK3 (PP.H4 0.90). 48 CpGs in 28 genes associated with DN risk, TNF methylation strongest; cell PM2.5 exposure reproduced TNF/NOS2 up and DUSP1 down; a two-gene nomogram gave AUC 0.766 (training) and 0.726 (external). The MR tests gene expression on DN, not PM2.5 on DN: the PM link is a database annotation, so the causal claim about pollution is not identified. Relevance: weak - no exposure measurement of any kind.

PAPERS.short: Alimu Kashi Xinjiang ExWAS elastic-net air pollution meteorology pulmonary tuberculosis 2026
PAPERS.title: Associations between air pollution, meteorology, and pulmonary tuberculosis risk in Kashi, China.
PAPERS.pm: Ambient PM10, PM2.5, NO2 and meteorology; source and averaging window not stated
PAPERS.endpoint: Pulmonary tuberculosis versus hospital non-TB controls
PAPERS.affil: First People's Hospital of Kashi, China; First People's Hospital of Kashi, China
PAPERS.n: TB cases from a surveillance platform compared with hospital non-TB controls in Kashi, Xinjiang, using ExWAS, adaptive elastic-net and XGBoost. Retained predictors: PM10 OR 1.013, PM2.5 OR 1.008, NO2 OR 1.018 (all p<0.0001), wind speed 0.983 and humidity 0.944; XGBoost ranked PM10 most important. No confidence intervals, increments, exposure windows or sample size are given in the abstract, and controls drawn from a hospital record system against cases from a separate platform build in selection bias; Kashi PM10 is dominated by Taklamakan dust, so PM10 also marks season and desert-dust episodes. Relevance: weak - a dust-dominated setting where PM10 sensors would be informative, but the design cannot carry a causal reading.

PAPERS.short: Singh German Diabetes Study long-term PM2.5 clamp insulin sensitivity albuminuria T1D T2D 2026
PAPERS.title: Associations of long-term exposure to air pollution with glucose homeostasis biomarkers and diabetes-related comorbidities in people with recent-onset type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
PAPERS.pm: Five-year mean PM2.5, PM10 and NO2 at residential address
PAPERS.endpoint: HbA1c, clamp insulin sensitivity, C-peptide secretion, insulin clearance, VO2max, albuminuria, DSPN
PAPERS.affil: German Diabetes Center, Heinrich Heine University Dusseldorf, Germany; German Diabetes Center, Germany
PAPERS.n: Cross-sectional analysis of 1,120 German Diabetes Study participants with recent-onset diabetes (417 T1D, 703 T2D), gold-standard clamp phenotyping. Per IQR PM2.5: T1D HbA1c exp(b) 1.07 (1.03-1.11), albuminuria 1.72 (1.34-2.20), VO2max 0.94 (0.89-0.99); T2D HbA1c 1.04 (1.01-1.06), insulin sensitivity b -0.42 (-0.82 to -0.03), insulin clearance 0.92 (0.87-0.98), albuminuria 1.71 (1.41-2.08), DSPN OR 1.53 (1.02-2.32). Many outcomes are tested without stated multiplicity control, and a single-time-point design cannot order exposure and disease progression. The IQR value is not in the abstract. Relevance: indirect - deep phenotyping makes this a strong mechanistic anchor; exposure is modelled, not measured.

PAPERS.short: Ali Somalia ecological time-series PM2.5 urbanization under-five mortality 1990-2023
PAPERS.title: Assessing Temporal Trends and Ecological Associations Between PM2.5 Exposure, Urbanization, and Under-Five Mortality in Somalia, 1990-2023: An Ecological Time-Series Analysis
PAPERS.pm: National annual population-weighted PM2.5 (modelled)
PAPERS.endpoint: Under-five mortality per 1,000 live births
PAPERS.n: Preprint. 34 annual national observations, Somalia 1990-2023, Theil-Sen trends and first-difference regression with Newey-West errors. PM2.5 rose 0.090 ug/m3 per year (0.042-0.143), urbanisation 0.661 points per year, and under-five mortality fell 2.30 per 1,000 per year. Year-on-year changes in PM2.5 were unrelated to under-five mortality (b 1.28, -8.81 to 11.36). With n=34 national points, conflict, drought and aid dominate mortality, and annual national PM2.5 for Somalia is itself a satellite-model product with little ground truth; the analysis has no power for an effect of the expected size. Relevance: weak - illustrates that national ecological series cannot detect PM effects, the opposite of what dense local monitoring provides.

PAPERS.short: Rana Bhopal indoor DustTrak PM1 PM2.5 PM10 TVOC 30 households seasonal 2026
PAPERS.title: Estimation of Emerging Indoor Air Pollutants and Associated Health Effects on Humans in the Capital City of Central India
PAPERS.pm: Indoor PM1, PM2.5, PM4, PM10, total PM by DustTrak photometer; TVOC
PAPERS.endpoint: Indoor concentrations by land-use zone and season; questionnaire morbidity
PAPERS.n: Preprint. 30 randomly selected Bhopal households across residential, commercial and industrial localities, monitored in winter, monsoon and summer with a DustTrak aerosol monitor (270 samples). Residential homes carried higher PM1-PM10 in most seasons; industrial areas peaked in summer; 258 of 270 samples were classed unhealthy, and morbidity prevalence was highest in industrial areas. No concentrations, effect estimates or photometer correction are given in the abstract; DustTrak readings are uncorrected optical mass and overestimate in humid, biomass-smoke-rich Indian homes. Morbidity is self-reported and not linked to measured exposure. Relevance: indirect - indoor optical photometry without gravimetric correction, the same error budget as low-cost indoor sensors.

PAPERS.short: Saz-Lara CarVasCLiMa Castilla-La Mancha cohort protocol air pollution satellite arterial stiffness
PAPERS.title: Impact of environmental factors on cardiovascular health in Castilla-La Mancha: the CarVasCLiMa cohort study protocol.
PAPERS.pm: Air pollution and climate from high-resolution satellite data with local monitoring stations
PAPERS.endpoint: Blood pressure, arterial stiffness, CRP over 2 years (planned)
PAPERS.affil: Universidad de Castilla-La Mancha, Spain; Universidad de Castilla-La Mancha, Spain
PAPERS.n: Protocol, no results. A representative urban, semi-urban and rural cohort in Castilla-La Mancha followed for 2 years, with air pollution and climate assigned from high-resolution satellite products supplemented by local stations, greenness by NDVI, and outcomes of blood pressure, arterial stiffness, C-reactive protein, quality of life and lifestyle. Sample size, pollutant list, spatial resolution and the exposure averaging windows are not given; two years is short for arterial-stiffness change, and rural Spain has few stations to anchor the satellite surface. Relevance: indirect - a rural cohort where co-located low-cost sensors could validate the satellite assignment before outcomes accrue.

PAPERS.short: Rehman Lahore GTWR satellite PM2.5 urban expansion climate 2015-2024
PAPERS.title: Urban expansion, seasonal climate and fine particulate matter in Lahore, Pakistan: a spatiotemporal analysis of regional environmental change (2015-2024)
PAPERS.pm: Satellite-derived PM2.5, 2015-2024
PAPERS.endpoint: Local climatic and urban-growth coefficients on PM2.5
PAPERS.n: Preprint. Satellite PM2.5 across Lahore 2015-2024 modelled with two geographically and temporally weighted regressions: climatic (1,400 point-seasons, R2 0.894) and socioeconomic (5,710 point-years, R2 0.562). Annual mean PM2.5 62.9-74.5 ug/m3, rising about 4.7% over the decade and spreading to the periphery, peaking in winter. Humidity was positive and rainfall negative; wind speed was dispersive in the north-east but positive on the western fringe, consistent with crop-burning smoke transport; built-up area, road density and population were strongest on the south-western periphery. The satellite product's own error in Lahore smog is not reported and GTWR coefficients are descriptive, not causal. Relevance: indirect - maps where a Lahore sensor network should be densified.

PAPERS.short: Angita Jhansi semi-arid campus automatic sensor PM2.5 PM10 annual cycle 2023
PAPERS.title: Year-Round Seasonal Variation of PM2.5 and PM10 at a Semi-Arid Institutional Campus Site in Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, India
PAPERS.pm: Continuous PM2.5 and PM10 from an automatic sensor, one campus site, 2023
PAPERS.endpoint: Seasonal and annual mean PM2.5, PM10
PAPERS.n: Preprint. One automatic sensor at a semi-arid campus in Jhansi, Bundelkhand, January-December 2023. Post-monsoon means were highest (PM2.5 63.55, PM10 190.63 ug/m3, November peak), monsoon lowest (33.17 and 99.52); annual PM2.5 37.45 ug/m3, under the Indian NAAQS of 40 but 7.5 times the WHO guideline, and PM10 113.00 against a standard of 60. ANOVA on 12 monthly means: F(3,8) 4.66 and 4.83. The instrument is unnamed, with no co-location, humidity correction or data-capture statistics, so the monsoon minimum and the PM2.5 standard compliance both sit inside unquantified sensor error. Relevance: direct - a single uncalibrated sensor reported as a compliance assessment, exactly the use the low-cost field warns against.

PAPERS.short: Wu Heyuan attention-LSTM SHAP hourly PM2.5 O3 forecasting persistence 2019-2023
PAPERS.title: Baseline-relative predictability of hourly PM2.5 and O3 in a low-emission South Chinese city: an attention-LSTM with feature attribution
PAPERS.pm: Hourly PM2.5 and O3 from two urban monitoring stations, 2019-2023
PAPERS.endpoint: Next-hour prediction R2 and RMSE; SHAP attribution
PAPERS.n: Preprint. Attention-LSTM on hourly observations from two Heyuan stations, 2019-2023, interpreted with SHAP. Test R2 0.9796-0.9877 for PM2.5 and 0.9921-0.9975 for O3, RMSE 1.28-2.02 and 1.77-2.83 ug/m3; the most recent pollutant observations dominated attributions, humidity and temperature contributed for O3. The authors themselves frame the result against persistence: at one-hour horizon a lag-1 baseline already achieves R2 near 0.95, and the abstract does not report the skill gain over it. Two stations in a low-emission city limit generality. Relevance: indirect - a useful cautionary example that high R2 in short-horizon PM forecasting mostly measures autocorrelation, relevant to edge-inference claims on sensor nodes.

PAPERS.short: Madej Poland 379 counties spatial Mundlak GAM mortality inequality PM2.5 2010-2025
PAPERS.title: Place-based structural disadvantage and mortality inequality across 379 Polish counties, 2010-2025: a spatial Mundlak analysis
PAPERS.pm: County-level PM2.5 (source not stated in the abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Age-sex-standardised all-cause mortality per 100,000
PAPERS.n: Preprint. 379 harmonised Polish counties, 2010-2025, spatial Mundlak GAMs separating between-county from within-county associations. Pre-COVID median between-county slope per SD: +30.2 deaths per 100,000 for PM2.5, against -26.1 for higher education and +29.4 for low education; these gradients persisted across windows, while within-county terms were unstable and sometimes reversed in pandemic-inclusive models. Leave-one-year-out validation showed weak temporal transportability, and the PM2.5 contribution contrast shrank after COVID-19. The between-county PM term is cross-sectional and collinear with Silesian coal-mining deprivation; no uncertainty on the slope is given in the abstract. Relevance: indirect - PM2.5 matches education in explaining Poland's mortality geography at ecological scale.

PAPERS.short: Huang UK Biobank CKD dementia multidomain risk factors air pollution null 2026
PAPERS.title: Disease susceptibility and risk of dementia in patients with chronic kidney disease: a prospective cohort study based on UK Biobank.
PAPERS.pm: UK Biobank residential air pollution estimates (LUR), one of many candidate factors
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident dementia
PAPERS.affil: West China Hospital of Sichuan University, China; West China Hospital of Sichuan University, China
PAPERS.n: 16,083 UK Biobank participants with CKD followed 13.8 years; 806 incident dementias. Cox models with inverse probability weighting, competing-risk and FDR correction screened lifestyle, clinical, social, device-use, environmental and sensory factors. Hypertension, diabetes, depression, hearing loss and low social activity raised risk; moderate activity and computer use lowered it. Air pollution showed no nominally significant association. With 806 events spread over dozens of exposures and UK Biobank's 2010 single-year LUR surfaces, power for a PM effect of the expected size (HR ~1.05-1.10 per few ug/m3) in a subgroup is low, so the null is uninformative rather than reassuring. Relevance: weak - a null by underpowered screening.

PAPERS.short: Alruqimi Alpine region multi-source machine learning daily NO2 PM10 PM2.5 estimation 2026
PAPERS.title: Multi-source machine learning for daily surface NO2, PM10, and PM2.5 estimation in Alpine region
PAPERS.pm: Daily surface PM2.5, PM10 and NO2 by multi-source machine learning (per title)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not recoverable
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: Crossref deposit without abstract, Atmospheric Environment. The title describes a multi-source machine-learning model producing daily surface NO2, PM10 and PM2.5 estimates across the Alpine region. No inputs, resolution, validation statistics, station counts or period can be recovered, and no finding is asserted here. Complex terrain with inversions and valley pooling is where satellite-ML PM products usually degrade, so the cross-validation design (spatial versus random) will decide how much the reported skill means. Relevance: potentially direct - an Alpine daily PM surface is a candidate fusion target for sensor networks in mountain valleys; recheck for the abstract in the weekly sweep.

PAPERS.short: Bittner Grieshop rural Malawi domestic biofuel emissions characterisation 2026
PAPERS.title: Characterizing emissions from diverse domestic biofuel uses in rural Malawi
PAPERS.pm: Emissions from household biofuel use (firewood and other biofuels) in field conditions (per title and abstract stub)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not recoverable
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: the Crossref deposit carries only the opening of the abstract, stating that household and small-scale industry energy in Malawi and similar sub-Saharan settings is almost entirely biofuel and that household air pollution is a primary concern. The title indicates emission characterisation across diverse domestic biofuel uses in rural Malawi. Emission factors, pollutants, instruments, sample size and any PM size information are not recoverable, and no finding is asserted. Relevance: potentially direct - field emission factors for non-cooking biofuel uses (brewing, brick and fish drying) are the missing source terms for household and community PM models in rural Africa; recheck for full abstract.

PAPERS.short: Jain air pollution redox proteomics oxidative modification review 2026
PAPERS.title: Air pollution leaves a redox-proteomic imprint: From shared inflammation to disease-specific vulnerability.
PAPERS.pm: Air pollution including PM (per title)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not recoverable
PAPERS.affil: Rungta College of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Research, India; Swami Atmanand Govt English Medium Model College, India
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: PubMed record without abstract, Redox Biology. The title frames a synthesis of air-pollution-induced redox-proteomic modifications, moving from shared inflammatory signatures to disease-specific vulnerability. Whether it is a narrative review or presents primary proteomic data, which pollutants or particle fractions are covered, and which tissues or diseases are addressed cannot be recovered, and no finding is asserted here. Relevance: indirect - such oxidative protein modifications are candidate biomarkers that would link oxidative-potential measurements on sensor or filter samples to biological effect in exposed people; recheck once the abstract is deposited.

PAPERS.short: Wang naphthalene SOA aerosol-organoid exposure platform glioma ALDH1A3 ferroptosis 2026
PAPERS.title: Secondary organic aerosol from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon modulates glioma proliferation.
PAPERS.pm: Photochemically generated naphthalene SOA delivered by an aerosol-organoid exposure platform
PAPERS.endpoint: Glioma cell and patient-derived organoid growth; ALDH1A3; ferroptosis
PAPERS.affil: Liangzhu Laboratory, Zhejiang University, China; Shanghai University, China
PAPERS.n: Naphthalene SOA, generated photochemically, was delivered at the air-liquid interface through a new aerosol-organoid exposure platform to patient-derived glioblastoma organoids and U87/U251 cells. Highly oxygenated SOA increased tumour-cell growth by upregulating ALDH1A3, which suppressed ferroptosis; high tumour ALDH1A3 tracked poor patient survival in public data. Dose, deposited mass, oxidation state metrics and effect magnitudes are not in the abstract, and SOA reaching glioma tissue in vivo is unshown, so this is a tumour-progression hypothesis rather than an exposure effect. Relevance: indirect - the exposure platform itself, delivering characterised aerosol to organoids, is the transferable contribution.

PAPERS.short: Madsen systematic review environmental risk factors acute myeloid leukemia GRADE 2026
PAPERS.title: Environmental risk factors for acute myeloid leukemia in adults, a systematic review.
PAPERS.pm: Ambient PM2.5, black carbon and secondary inorganic aerosol components among other environmental exposures
PAPERS.endpoint: Adult acute myeloid leukaemia incidence
PAPERS.affil: Aalborg University Hospital, Denmark; Aalborg University Hospital, Denmark
PAPERS.n: Systematic review with risk-of-bias and GRADE assessment, 6,685 records screened, 15 studies from 11 populations included; no meta-analysis. Seven studies were high risk of bias. Of those not at high risk, associations appeared in four, for air pollution (PM2.5, black carbon, secondary inorganic aerosol, ammonium, NOx, nitrate) and farm residency. Certainty was low for air pollution and very low for residential benzene, chlorinated water, radiation, industry proximity and power lines. Four studies supporting the PM signal is thin, and AML is rare, so exposure misclassification biases toward the null. Relevance: indirect - PM remains the best-supported environmental AML exposure, at low certainty.

PAPERS.short: Ni GBD 2021 otitis media macroeconomic burden value of lost welfare PM secondhand smoke
PAPERS.title: The global macroeconomic burden of otitis media and its modifiable risk factors.
PAPERS.pm: GBD 2021 particulate matter risk factor (ambient and household)
PAPERS.endpoint: DALYs and value of lost welfare attributable to otitis media
PAPERS.affil: Fifth Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, China; Fifth Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: GBD 2021 DALYs for otitis media in 183 countries converted to value of lost welfare against PPP-adjusted GDP. Total burden was US$13.82 billion (0.009% of world GDP), highest in sub-Saharan Africa (0.016%) and Somalia (>0.042%). Of three modifiable risks (secondhand smoke, low birth weight/short gestation, particulate matter), secondhand smoke contributed most, US$0.15 billion; the PM-attributable share is not stated in the abstract. The analysis inherits GBD exposure surfaces and risk curves without independent uncertainty, and value-of-welfare metrics scale with income. Relevance: weak - PM is a minor attributed risk for this endpoint; no new exposure information.
